‘Lando’ floods Nueva Vizcaya villages, leaves 1 dead
By Ben Moses Ebreo

BAMBANG, Nueva Vizcaya, Oct 19 (PNA) -- Typhoon ‘Lando’s’ rains on Sunday brought flashfloods and landslides in several barangays of the 15 municipalities of the province, isolating several towns and communities.

Flashfloods which struck low-lying areas in the province brought in additional evacuees in community centers Sunday afternoon due to the swelling of rivers and irrigation canals.

Commuters going in and outside the province were stranded for more than five hours along the national highway in barangays Almaguer North and Macate in this town as the stretch was under hip-deep floodwaters.

“Commuters, especially those carrying light vehicles were only allowed to pass after the flood subsided in the morning,” said Police Senior Supt. John Luglug, police provincial chief.

Initial report from the Provincial Disaster Risk Reeduction Management Office9PDRRMO) said an unidentified baby died after it was carried away by strong flood waters in Bayombong town.

Close to 800 families were temporarily evacuated in various community centers due to rampaging floodwaters.

Power is still cut off in the towns of Kayapa, Ambaguio and Kasibu as landslides blocked major roads to these upland municipalities.

“We are doing restoration works since yesterday but we cannot proceed in some areas because of landslides,” said engineer Narciso Salunat, Nueva Vizcaya Electric Cooperative(NUVELCO) manager.

Major landslides were reported in barangays Antutot , Poblacion and Dulli in Kasibu town, barangay Runruno in Quezon town and barangay Bitnong in Dupax del Norte town.

Provincial officials said heavy equipments are now focusing their efforts in clearing a major landslide in Kasibu town.

Initial report from the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office of Bambang town said 22 houses were partially damaged while one has been totally destroyed due to strong winds and floodwaters spawned by typhoon ‘Lando.’

The Alfonso Castaneda National High School(ACNHS) in Alfonso Castaneda town was reportedly in total wreck due to the typhoon. (PNA)

The majority of what you will hear in today’s message is from the New York Times best seller – The Circle Marker by Ptr. Mark Batterson. 

I. The Circle Marker is a book about prayer. It’s a book about phenomenal answers to prayer. Recently, I’ve been rereading George Muller’s booklet Answers to Prayer as well. That little booklet brings me to tears! I encourage you to download it for free (pdf file). 

Miracles are the byproduct of prayers that were prayed either by you or for you. For whatever reason, God has determined that certain manifestations of His power will only be displayed in response to believing prayer.  Jesus said – “this one comes out only by prayer and fasting”.

As John Wesley famously said – “God does nothing on earth except in response to believing prayer.”

II. Psalm 126:1-6 – (NKJV) “When the LORD brought back the captivity of Zion, we were like those who dream. 2 Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, "The LORD has done great things for them." 3 The LORD has done great things for us, and we are glad. 4 Bring back our captivity, O LORD, As the streams in the South. 5 Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy. 6 He who continually goes forth weeping, Bearing seed for sowing, Shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, Bringing his sheaves with him.”

One of the themes of our World Conference in Canada came from Dr. George Hill– “Dream, live the dream, and dream again!”

Acts 2:17 tells us – “In the last days, God says, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams.”

Prayers, the right kind of prayers, are dreams put into words, and directed toward God! What are your dreams today? What do you dream of? Do you dream of the day that your husband, your wife, your entire household are all serving God with their whole heart? Do you dream of the day that you can give a P100,000 to the work of the Lord? How about a million?! Do you dream of the day that you’ll have your own business, or your own home, or your own car? Do you dream of the day that God will use you mightily and perhaps you’ll speak before thousands?

What are your hopes and what are your dreams? Dream big dreams for God! Pray big prayers to your God!

Smith Wigglesworth said -  “Bold prayers honor God and God honors bold prayers”.

I once heard the true story of a poor Filipino pastor who came to a certain well-known evangelist who was quite well known for getting incredible miraculous answers to prayer. The poor pastor came to the evangelist and asked, “Would you pray for me that God would give me a car?”. “What kind of car would you like?,” he asked. “Any old car kahit karag karag na lang!” Angrily the evangelist answered – “My God isn’t a karag karag God! You go fix your karag karag faith first and come back when you know how to ask!” Ouch! The point being that all our prayers should honor God. And the answer to those prayers should bring glory to Him.  

III. I want to tell you today that you can literally live a life of miracles if you will learn how to pray through. If you will learn how to pray and not give up! If you will learn the secret of the circle maker! 

The Jewish legend of the circle maker is the story of a Jewish prophet by the name of Honi who lived about 100 years BC. Israel was in a terrible drought, people were nearly dying of hunger. The story is told that Honi took a long staff and drew a circle in the dust in the streets of Jerusalem. People came out of their homes to see what the prophet would do. It was then that the prophet knelt down in the middle of that circle and cried out with a loud voice to Jehovah, “God I will not leave this circle until You send rain”. In a few moments, it began to sprinkle down little droplets of rain. Honi prayed again – "Not for such rain have I prayed, but for rain that will fill the cisterns, pits, and caverns." It began to rain with great violence. So much so, that it began to flood! Honi never moved. He prayed again, "Not for such rain have I prayed, but for rain of goodwill, blessing, and graciousness." Then it rained in steady moderation.

Ptr. Mark Batterson draws a parallel between the story of Honi, the walls of Jericho, and the need for you and I to circle our “impossibilities” in prayer with the promises of God. That if we will pray and not give up circling the problem with prayer, praise, and thanksgiving as the Israelites did the walls of Jericho, sooner or later those walls will come down and we will see God move miraculously on our behalf!

IV. Luke 18:1 – “Then Jesus told His disciples a parable to show them that they should always pray and not give up. 2 He said: "In a certain town, there was a judge who neither feared God nor cared about men. 3 And there was a widow in that town who kept coming to him with the plea, 'Grant me justice against my adversary.' 4 "For some time, he refused. But finally he said to himself, 'Even though I don't fear God or care about men, 5 yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will see that she gets justice, so that she won't eventually wear me out with her coming!'" 6 And the Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says. 7 And will not God bring about justice for His chosen ones, who cry out to Him day and night? Will He keep putting them off? 8 I tell you, He will see that they get justice, and quickly. However, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on the earth?".

“Faith” in this parable is obviously shown NOT as instant answers to prayer but as persistence in prayer! Refusing to give up! Like Hannah, the mother of Samuel, crying out to God year after year refusing to take no for an answer until God granted her request! And she gave birth to a prophet! Like King Hezekiah who turned his face to the wall and cried out to God for 15 more years to be added to his life, and God granted his request even after the prophet Isaiah had prophesied that he would die.

“Will He find faith on the earth?” Or will we have given up? 

Miracles happen when people pray for the seemingly impossible and when we encircle those impossibilities in prayer and refuse to stop praying until the impossibilities become realities! God is glorified! He LOVES to do the impossible!

V. As we grow older, one of two things happens - either we dream bigger and bigger, believe bigger and grow bigger in our faith, OR we live out of the past. Living in the past, allowing the past failures, frustrations, and disappointments to dictate to us our future. Are you dwelling on the past or the future?

You will either dream ever increasing, ever growing dreams for the glory of a BIG GOD, or you will settle into a life of mediocrity and excuses as to why God doesn’t do miracles anymore! IF we are indeed experiencing answers to prayer, miracles, our faith will grow. If our faith grows, our dreams will grow! If our dreams grow, our prayers will grow! We will be like Caleb of old who at the age of 85 boldly declared “Give me this mountain”!

Dream, live the dream, and dream again! Either God is growing ever bigger in your view / life or ever smaller, ever more limited! Imagination, dreams, and genuine faith-filled prayer, all speak the same language. The language of possibility.

VI. What is your Jericho?
What are the seemingly impossible things you've hoped and prayed for? Are you still circling them in prayer? Don't stop until those walls fall down! We MUST DEFINE clearly what we're believing God for. Jesus asked the blind man “What is it that you want?”. If faith is the certainty or assurance of things hoped for, then the opposite of faith (doubt and unbelief) is the uncertainty and lack of assurance of what you're hoping for! What do you really want?! Are you sure? 

Well-defined prayers are a sign of well-developed faith. 

Defining it creates a certainty! A focus. The more faith you have, the more specific your prayers will be. The more specific your prayers are, the more God is glorified in answering them.

Identify your Jericho. What are the promises God has given you?
Circle your Jericho with those promises continually! Sis. Jemima Mortel did and she got the answer! Sis. Ana Balao did, and she got the answer! What are you believing God for today? 

VI. What if the Israelites had only circled Jerusalem for six days instead of seven? Would the walls have fallen down?  What if they said to one another, “You know, this isn’t working. In fact, this is just foolish, we’re just dreaming here! It doesn’t make any sense at all!”  What if Daniel in Daniel Chapter 10 had only prayed for 14 days instead of 21? Would the answer have come? It’s doubtful.

There’s something about persistence! There’s something about circling your mountain with the promise. Daniel had read in the scriptures of Israel’s deliverance, and therefore went to prayer! He prayed through! 
He prayed until he knew that he had the answer! 

Hebrews 6:12 tells us that it’s through – “faith and patience” that we inherit the promises! Abraham waited 25 long years but never gave up his dream! Joseph spent 13 years in prison. He was able to endure because he had a dream!

Have you given up on your dreams?! May God resurrect them today! God is in the resurrection business! God is in the “impossibilities” business! Making all things possible to them that believe.

Maybe you’re saying “But pastor, my faith is so weak.” That’s alright. All it takes is the faith as a grain of a mustard seed! Do you have just a tiny little bit of faith?! Well, it can grow! Water it with the Word, water it in prayer! And that little mustard seed faith will become mountain moving faith!
